newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Wah Shing sees continue margin squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Wah Shing sees continue margin squeeze.

text.p: Over-capacity in the global toy manufacturing industry will continue to squeeze profit margins of toy maker Wah Shing International Holdings Ltd, company officials said on Friday.
"There is a continuing pressure on margins. The over-capacity in the toy industry is causing a squeeze on all manufacturers," Wah Shing deputy chairman Howard Gorges told Reuters in an interview.

But Gorges said the Hong Kong-based group, which makes toys under Orignal Equipment Manufacturing (OEM) arrangements, had faired better than its listed competitors and continued to see profits and high turnover.
"We are looking for the same growth in turnover," added managing director Kwok Choi Lo, who said demand for the company's toys was expected to remain healthy in 1997.

For the financial year ended December 31, 1996, Wah Shing's turnover grew 12 percent to about HK$1 billion on improved sales, notably in the United States. Net profit however fell 19 percent to HK$102.8 million.
Lo said he expected U.S sales to improve this year but saw only a "slight improvement" in Europe.

Last year Wah Shing's U.S. sales grew 45 percent while European sales slipped 22 percent, a drop attributed to market saturation in some products launched by its customers and weaker European currencies.
Lo said Wah Shing had no diversifaction plans.
"We will continue to manufacture toys for the OEMs. In fact our toys are very diversified ranging from children to entertainment products," Lo said.
Wah Shing has ventured into making polyresin toys and the collector gift market, where sales in 1997 are expected to increase four times from about HK$2 million last year.
Despite the prevailing squeeze on margins, Wah Shing intends to expand its market share, Lo said.

"Ours is a market share strategy. We will continue to grow. To be large to reduce the risk of the unstable product performance of customers," he said, adding that international customers tend to want to deal with bigger manufacturers.
China is the company's main toy production site and no alternative sites are being sought, Lo said, dismissing any fears of over-exposure to the mainland.
Wah Shing belongs to Hong Kong South China Holdings Ltd.
